flasher.title: Flash your ESP32-C5
flasher.intro: Choose a compiled .bin image from your computer, or use the bundled ESP32-C5 MicroPython image. The browser flashes the board directly over Web Serial.
flasher.imageHelp: For a merged image, use one .bin at 0x0. For separate bootloader, partition and app images, add each file with its build's own flash offset.
flasher.microPythonImageHelp: Choose the firmware for your board. Both included full .bin images are written at 0x2000; you can also choose your own full .bin (not an .app-bin).
flasher.sparkfunOnly: This option is for the SparkFun Thing Plus ESP32-C5 board. For Pulsar C5, select ESP32_GENERIC_C5.
flasher.offsetHelp: Use the offsets from your build output. Common ESP32-C5 offsets are bootloader 0x2000, partitions 0x8000 and app 0x10000, but your project may differ.
flasher.stepCable: Connect the board with a USB data cable and close any other serial monitor.
flasher.stepPort: Press Flash firmware and choose the board's serial port.
flasher.stepBoot: If connection fails, hold BOOT, press RESET, release RESET, then release BOOT and try again.
flasher.warning: Flashing erases the sectors covered by these images. Do not unplug the board while writing.
flasher.eraseAllWarning: The entire flash will be erased, including saved .py scripts and board data. The selected firmware will then be written. Do not unplug the board during this process.
flasher.unsupported: This page needs HTTPS or localhost and a browser with Web Serial, such as Chrome or Edge on a desktop computer.
flasher.success: Firmware written. The board was reset.
flasher.successManualReset: Firmware written. Press RESET on the board to start it.
flasher.logEmpty: The connection log will appear here.

phase.error: Check the message and try again.

01.title: Change RGB brightness
01.try: Change BRIGHTNESS from 40 to 15, download the sketch and upload it from Arduino IDE. Disconnect the serial monitor first.
01.expect: The rainbow continues at a lower brightness. The monitor displays chip information.

02.title: Compare two speeds
02.try: With the sketch uploaded and the terminal connected, send blink 200, then blink 800. Read how command() handles the text.
02.expect: The LED changes from fast to slow blinking; the monitor confirms each mode.

P1.title: Test the BOOT input
P1.try: Change the pressed interval from 100 to 50 ms, upload the sketch, then hold BOOT.
P1.expect: The user LED blinks faster while BOOT is held; the monitor reports the button state.

P2.title: Mix a colour, then dim it
P2.try: Upload the sketch, connect the console and send rgb 255 80 0. Compare level 20 with level 100.
P2.expect: The LED stays orange while its brightness changes; off turns it dark.

P3.title: Compare raw and calibrated readings
P3.try: Move the potentiometer near its midpoint and locate both ADC reads in the sketch.
P3.expect: The monitor reports a raw count and a millivolt value for the same position.

P4.title: Count the on-board devices
P4.try: Run the scanner and compare its addresses with the five expected sensors in the guide.
P4.expect: The serial monitor lists the addresses that answered on the board's I²C bus.

P5.title: Check that a file survives reset
P5.try: Run the sketch with a FAT32 microSD card, then press RST twice and read the log again.
P5.expect: Each boot appends one more line to /pulsar.txt without deleting earlier lines.

P6.title: Test the UART loopback
P6.try: Join TX0 to RX0, upload the sketch and send hello UART. Then remove the jumper and send it again.
P6.expect: The first message returns as loopback: hello UART; the second no longer returns.

D2.title: See how the light graph is built
D2.try: Find DevLabDDP::Master in the sketch, then follow the ADC reading into drawGraph().
D2.expect: The OLED plots the last 126 samples while the serial monitor prints raw values.

O1.title: Turn on the OLED
O1.try: Upload o1-oled.ino with only the SSD1306 connected to QWIIC.
O1.expect: The screen shows Pulsar C5 and OLED ready.

00.title: Check the REPL
00.try: After installing the firmware, connect the serial port at 115200 baud and send the test command.
00.expect: The console displays MicroPython OK and returns to the >>> prompt. The first .py file appears in lesson 01.

01.title: Change RGB brightness
01.try: Change BRIGHTNESS from 40 to 15 and press Run on board. Press Stop before editing again.
01.expect: The LED cycles through the same colours at a lower brightness.

02.title: Change the LED timing
02.try: Change sleep_ms(12) to sleep_ms(30) and run the file again.
02.expect: The external LED fades up and down more slowly.

P1.title: Test the BOOT input
P1.try: Run gpio.py, then change the pressed interval from 100 to 50 ms and hold BOOT.
P1.expect: The user LED blinks faster while BOOT is held; the REPL reports its state.

P2.title: Mix a colour, then dim it
P2.try: Run rgb_mixer.py, then send rgb 255 80 0, level 20 and level 100 in the terminal.
P2.expect: The LED stays orange while its brightness changes; off turns it dark.

P3.title: Compare ADC and voltage
P3.try: Run adc.py and turn the potentiometer while comparing read_u16() with read_uv().
P3.expect: The 16-bit scaled value and approximate millivolts follow the knob.

P4.title: Find the on-board sensors
P4.try: Run i2c_scan.py and compare the reported addresses with the five devices in the guide.
P4.expect: The REPL lists the devices that answered on GPIO2/GPIO3.

P5.title: Check that the file keeps its data
P5.try: Install sdcard.py on the board, insert a FAT32 card, then run microsd.py twice and read /sd/pulsar.txt after each run.
P5.expect: Each run appends a line without deleting the earlier one.

P6.title: Test the UART loopback
P6.try: Bridge GPIO11 to GPIO12, run uart_loopback.py and send hello UART in the terminal.
P6.expect: The script prints loopback: hello UART; without the jumper it reports no response.

D2.title: Plot light on the OLED
D2.try: Install ssd1306.py, run oled_light.py, then cover and illuminate the TEMT6000.
D2.expect: The terminal identifies device 0x0102 and the OLED graph follows the light.

O1.title: Turn on the OLED
O1.try: Install ssd1306.py, then run oled.py with only the display connected.
O1.expect: The screen shows Pulsar C5 and MicroPython.
